scenes.name: Punk-rock británico
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: La gira de los Ramones de 1976 contagia a Inglaterra, donde el punk es combinación de moda y paro: la Gran Bretaña de Thatcher, con las ciudades industriales devastadas, convierte el «punk» en algo mucho más serio que lo que pretendían los Ramones. Malcolm McLaren inventa el sonido (Sex Pistols, «los Ramones con heroína y valium») y la imagen. The Clash, los más intelectuales (London Calling, Sandinista); Damned, Generation X, Buzzcocks (inventores del punk-pop), Vibrators. En Australia, Radio Birdman y los Saints. La segunda ola (GBH, UK Subs, Neurotics, New Model Army, Stiff Little Fingers) y el punk anarquista (Crass, Discharge, Rudimentari Peni, Subhumans).
scenes.family: Punk, new wave, hardcore y noise

mentions.author: Piero Scaruffi
mentions.text: …were other important scenes. The Australian scene was closely related to the British scene, but the results were different, as Radio Birdman and the Saints (two of the greatest punk bands of all times) opted for the raw and wild style of Stooges and MC5 rather than the Sex Pistol's primal assault. podcast.title: Brisbane Origin and Style (Late 1973/1974)
podcast.body: Originating from Brisbane, Australia, The Saints began as Kid Galahad and the Eternals around late 1973 or 1974. Influenced by The Stooges and The Velvet Underground, they developed a distinctive fast-paced style, as they found they "couldn't play slow." By late 1975, they were performing their songs "really, really fast." "A band called The Saints released a rough, raw garage band like single that rocked in an entirely new way. They had obviously got their hands on some stooge's and velvet underground records."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Impact on UK Music Scene
podcast.body: The Saints, along with the Sex Pistols and The Clash, were identified as one of three bands that "changed the music forever in the UK," particularly after their single "(I'm) Stranded" caused a media sensation there in 1976. "Because of that media freak out, three bands changed the music forever in the UK, the sex pistols, the clash, and the Saints."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Predecessor to The Saints (Late 1973/1974)
xref.body: The Saints initially started "goofing around" under the name Kid Galahad and the Eternals by late 1973 or 1974, before developing their fast-paced style. "And they started goofing around under the name Kid Galaad and the Eternals by late 1973 or 1974."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Impact on UK Music Scene (1975)
xref.body: The Sex Pistols were identified as one of three bands, alongside The Clash and The Saints, that "changed the music forever in the UK," following the media frenzy over The Saints' 1976 single. Their emergence in England coincided with the germination of punk rock in New York by 1975. "Because of that media freak out, three bands changed the music forever in the UK, the sex pistols, the clash, and the Saints."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
